proof.text:
Use the notation $J,P,K,Q$ in the statement and work in the four categories of ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves. For a pro-etale module sheaf $G$ on $V$ and an etale $W\to T$, the direct-image formulas give
$$(\nu_{T,*}QG)(W)=G(W\times_TV)=(K\nu_{V,*}G)(W).$$
Both restriction maps along $h:W'\to W$ are induced by $h\times_T\mathrm{id}_V$, so these identities define the natural isomorphism $\delta:R_2\to R_1$ specified in the statement. They respect coefficients: both constant-ring maps send $r\in A$ to the constant section $r$ on $W\times_TV$. Thus $\delta$ and its inverse are maps of module sheaves, not just maps of underlying sets.

proof.text: Let $W\to V$ be etale and regard $W$ also as etale over $T$; $j$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], so the etale restriction-unit theorem applies to $j$. Since $j$ is an open immersion, hence a monomorphism, the projection $\mathrm{pr}:W\times_TV\to W$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\varphi_0=(\mathrm{id}_W,\mathrm{str})$: the entire image of $W\to T$ lies in $V$. Use this canonical identification throughout. Etale side: clause (2) of the etale restriction-unit theorem makes $\rho_F\circ e_F(W)$ the restriction of $F$ along $\mathrm{pr}$, hence the identity under this identification; $\rho$ is natural, so it commutes with every scalar endomorphism and the same holds for module sheaves. Pro-etale side, with the identification $\sigma$ of the statement: by the pro-etale inverse-image definition the adjunction $P\dashv Q$ is that of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction], whose bijection is the composite of Stacks 00VE (lemma-adjoints-u) and sheafification; in 00VE the adjunct of $\alpha$ is $u^p\alpha\circ c(\mathrm{id}_{u(U)})$ (lemma-recover), so the unit $f_M(W):M(W)\to(PM)(W\times_TV)$ is the coprojection indexed by $(W,\mathrm{id})$ followed by $u_pM\to(u_pM)^\#$. By clause (1) of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], $\sigma^{-1}$ at $W\times_TV\to V$ is the coprojection indexed by the initial pair $(W\times_TV\to T,\varphi_0')$ followed by the same sheafification map. The arrow $\mathrm{pr}$ goes from this pair to $(W,\mathrm{id})$ in $\mathcal I$, since $u(\mathrm{pr})\varphi_0'=\mathrm{id}$ on both projections, so the colimit relation gives $\iota_{(W,\mathrm{id})}(m)=\iota_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathrm{pr}^*m)$. Thus $\sigma\circ f_M(W)$ is restriction along $\mathrm{pr}$, the identity under the identification, for $M=\nu_T^*F$. The unit is natural, hence commutes with scalars. No quasi-compactness is used, and the identification of $P$ is exactly the one fixed in the statement.

proof.text:
Evaluate the equation of step 3 at $W\to T$ and use step 4. By step 1 the component of $\delta$ is also the identity on the same sections. Thus, with the prescribed restriction identifications, the equation becomes
$$\nu_{V,*}(\gamma_F)(W)\circ\eta^V_{JF}(W)
=c_{\nu_T^*F}(W)\circ J(\eta^T_F)(W).$$
Compose on the left with $\nu_{V,*}(a_F)(W)$. Since $a_F\gamma_F=\mathrm{id}$, this gives exactly the asserted unit equation at $W$. This works for every etale $W\to V$, so it is an equality of sheaf morphisms: a natural transformation is determined by its object components. All these components are module homomorphisms by steps 1--4; the equality therefore holds in the stated module category. Applying the component equality to $s\in F(W\to T)$ gives the sectionwise formulation, and conversely equality on all such sections gives the component equality.
